notes.text: These are new single-family houses completed that year in that region, including houses built for rent. They describe how houses were being built, not any one house.
Counts before 1999 include a 3.3 percent upward adjustment for houses built without permits in areas that issue permits, so house counts before and after 1999 are not strictly comparable.
The Census counts slabs together with other foundations such as piers and pilings, so this is “slab or other”, never slab alone.
Vinyl siding was not counted separately until 1992. Before then it sits inside “other”, with aluminum, block and stone.
Fiber cement was not counted separately until 2005. Before then it sits inside “other”.
Aluminum siding is counted inside “other”, with block and stone.
From 2014 the Census stopped publishing oil separately; oil and kerosene are counted with “other or none”.
Gas includes bottled gas and propane as well as natural gas.
Heat pumps were not counted separately until 1978.

Floors are counted two ways: through 2008, 1 story, 2 or more, and split-level; from 2009, split-level and 1½-story houses count as 2 stories and 3 or more is separate. Only “1 story” is roughly comparable across the change.
Garages for 3 or more cars were counted with 2-car garages until 1992.
These are survey estimates. Sampling error is larger for older years, for single regions and for small categories; “withheld” marks cells the Census did not publish.
